title: Anatomy: how a board becomes a map
goal: Understand how a board file written by an agent becomes a map you can explore, and how your own notes stay safe when the agent writes a new version.

includes: Opening, checking, and showing a board file
Exploring the map, the inspector, walkthroughs, and lessons
Where your notes, links, and card positions are kept, and how they survive an updated board
excludes: How the agent decides what to write: the app only reads the file
How the map routes lines and places labels in detail

groups.label: Outside the app
groups.description: Files and tools that the app reads but does not control.

groups.label: In the browser tab
groups.description: Code that runs in this tab. Nothing is sent over the network.

groups.label: Your layer
groups.description: Everything you add or change. The agent's file never overwrites it.

components.label: Your agent
components.summary: Any coding agent you already use. You ask it to explain a plan, feature, or project, and it writes a board file.
components.explanation: Anatomy has no AI inside it. The **How to make a board** button gives you a prompt, the authoring guide, and the JSON Schema to hand to your agent.
inputs: Material you allow it to read

components.label: Board file
components.summary: A JSON file that lists parts, connections, open questions, and walkthroughs, each with a label that says where it came from.
components.explanation:
The file is **data only**. The app never runs anything from it, and file paths in it are shown as text, never opened.

Every part and connection carries a source: an agent explanation, an agent proposal, a documented plan, or something you said.
inputs: Written by an agent or a person

components.label: Export file
components.summary: One file that holds a board together with your notes, links, and card positions. It is the only backup that survives clearing the browser.
outputs: A file you can keep, move, or share

components.label: Validator
components.summary: Checks the file's size, format, fields, and IDs, and that every connection points at a real part. A broken file is rejected with a list of problems.
components.explanation:
Checks run in order: size (at most 1,000,000 bytes), JSON syntax, format and version, the shape of every field, then cross-references.

A rejected file never replaces the board that is already open. A board with more than 15 parts opens with a warning, and one with more than 60 is rejected.
outputs: A checked board, or a list of problems

components.label: App state
components.summary: One central store that holds the open board, your layer, the selection, and the walkthrough step. Every screen reads from it.
components.explanation: Every change goes through one pure function that takes the old state and an action and returns the new state. This keeps the map, the inspector, and storage in agreement.

components.label: Map
components.summary: Draws each part as a card and each connection as a labeled line. You can drag cards, pan, zoom, and draw your own links.
components.explanation:
While you drag a card, only that card's lines are redrawn, as simple curves. After you drop it, one full pass routes every line around the cards and places the labels so they do not overlap.

Groups are the shaded areas behind the cards. They grow and move with the cards inside them.

components.label: Inspector
components.summary: The panel on the right. It explains the selected part or connection in plain English, with its source and any open questions.
components.explanation: It leads with what the part does. The longer explanation, open items, citations, your links, and your notes sit in sections that you can open and close. A section opens by itself when something in it needs review.

components.label: Walkthrough player
components.summary: Plays a scenario from the board one step at a time. Each step has a caption and lights up the parts and connections it is about.

components.label: Lessons
components.summary: Hand-built interactive lessons that ship with the app. A board can attach one to a part by its ID.
components.explanation: A board only names a lesson, it never contains one. If the app does not know the name, the board still opens and shows a warning.
inputs: A lesson ID on a part

components.label: Update review
components.summary: When you open a newer version of a board you already have, it compares the two and lists what was added, removed, and changed.
components.explanation: Existing cards stay where you put them, and new cards get a free spot. Notes on changed parts are marked **possibly outdated**, and notes on removed parts are marked **needs relinking**.

components.label: Your notes and links
components.summary: Your notes, questions, links between cards, and card positions. They are kept apart from the agent's board.
components.explanation: Each note remembers a short fingerprint of what it was attached to. When the board changes, the app compares fingerprints to tell whether the note still fits. The app never deletes or moves a note by itself.

components.label: Browser storage
components.summary: Keeps your boards and your layer in this browser, so they survive a reload. Home and Work are two separate stores.
components.explanation: Saving happens a moment after each change. The toolbar shows whether the work is saved. If saving fails, the work stays on screen and the app offers an export.
outputs: The same data after a reload

relationships.label: clicks and drops
relationships.explanation: A drag sends one change when you drop the card, not one per frame. Pressing Escape during a drag puts the card back.

items.text: Browser data can be cleared, so an export file is the only safe backup.
The app checks the shape of a board, not whether its content is true. Source labels tell you how much to trust each part.
There is no undo yet for moving a card. Whether it is needed depends on how often cards get moved by mistake.
Should the map stop you from dropping one card on top of another?

steps.caption: Your agent writes a board file.
You open the file. The validator checks it before anything changes on screen.
The checked board goes into the app state, together with any card positions saved earlier.
The map draws a card for each part and a line for each connection.
You click a card. The inspector explains it in plain English.

scenarios.title: Add a note and keep it

steps.caption: In the inspector, you write a note or a question about the selected part.
You drag a card or draw a link. That also goes into your layer, not into the board.
A moment later, your layer is saved in this browser.
To keep it anywhere else, you export one file with the board and your layer.

scenarios.title: The agent writes a new version

steps.caption: Your agent writes a new version of a board you already have, with the same ID.
The validator checks it like any other file.
The app sees a board with the same ID and starts an update review.
Your notes are checked against the new board by fingerprint. Notes on changed parts are marked for review. None are deleted.
You open a file with a connection that points at a part that does not exist.
The validator lists the problem and stops. The board that was already open stays on screen.
